assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit QED made a superconducting artificial atom strongly coupled to a single microwave photon in a resonator, opening dispersive readout, quantum-nondemolition measurement, and the architecture used in essentially all superconducting quantum processors. It is a clean new regime of light-matter physics (strong coupling on a chip) that became an enabling platform, and the experiments are reproduced in dozens of laboratories. As a member working in this field I note the conflict-of-interest issue below; on the merits it ranks first.
assessment.attribution: Proposal (Schoelkopf's group and Wallraff's group made the 2004 Nature experiment with the Yale proposal of Blais, Huang, Wallraff, Girvin and Schoelkopf) credits the three names. The supplied list cannot include Girvin, Huang or Majer; Blais is the principal theory architect, and Schoelkopf and Wallraff the experimental leads. A fair three-person configuration is available, but I am uncertain about how the committee will weigh theory versus experiment and the contributions of Yale colleagues not on the list.
assessment.maturity: Mature: more than twenty years of confirmation, extension to ultrastrong coupling, bosonic codes, and multi-lab quantum-computing devices. Timing is good, though the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits is closely related and the committee may want some distance.
uncertainties: Overlap in subject with the 2025 prize and with my own research field and WACQT directorship, which may require recusal or at least careful discussion.
Credit beyond the three listed names (for example Girvin, Huang, and Yale co-authors) is not resolved here and my recollection of priority details is not independently verified.
Whether the committee judges the discovery to be the physics of strong coupling or the architecture/technology.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Katori's magic-wavelength proposal and Ye's demonstration of Sr lattice clocks led to optical clocks with fractional uncertainties at the 10^-18 level, redefining what precision measurement can do and enabling tests of fundamental constants, relativistic redshift across millimetres, and a likely redefinition of the second. A very clean physical idea with exceptional experimental execution.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the optical lattice clock and magic wavelength and made the first Sr demonstration; Ye's group drove it to record accuracy and many applications. Two laureates seems a defensible configuration; Hall and Hansen were already honoured in 2005 for the comb, and other clock work (e.g. ion clocks of Wineland, already 2012) is separate.
assessment.maturity: Mature and reproduced in many national laboratories with consistent results; the second redefinition is still pending, which makes the timing reasonable but not urgent.
uncertainties: Whether ion-clock and comb prizes already awarded make this seem incremental to some members.
Exact claims of priority between early lattice-clock proposals are from memory, not verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The prediction of the quantum spin Hall effect and Z2 topological insulators by Kane and Mele, and the experimental observation of helical edge transport in HgTe wells by Molenkamp's group, opened a major field of topological electronic matter. The conceptual originality is high and the experiment confirmed a sharp prediction.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele are decisive for theory; Molenkamp for the first experimental realization (with Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang's theory proposal not on this entry). The three listed names make a clean configuration, though omission of Zhang is a known unresolved allocation issue (I rely on memory and cannot verify it here).
assessment.maturity: Well confirmed across many materials and techniques, widely cited and stable, although the 2016 prize recognized topological phase transitions, which may be thought of as nearby.
uncertainties: Credit for the HgTe proposal and 3D topological insulators (Moore, Balents, Fu, Hasan) is not in this candidate.
The relation to the 2016 prize may reduce appetite for a second topology prize.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Controlled cold atoms and trapped ions as platforms for quantum information and simulation: Cirac and Zoller's proposals for gates and simulators, Blatt's ion-based implementations, and Bloch's optical-lattice simulators. This is foundational physics that has become a general platform, and is a natural complement to the superconducting-circuit work I know.
assessment.attribution: Cirac and Zoller are the theoretical originators of the gate and simulator proposals, and Bloch is the leading experimentalist for optical-lattice simulation, so I propose these three. This omits Blatt, whose ion-trap implementations are decisive for the quantum-computing half of the candidate, so the allocation is a genuine judgement. Wineland and Haroche (2012) and others are not credited here.
assessment.maturity: Highly mature, repeatedly confirmed in many laboratories; the interplay with the 2012 prize and the 2022 prize on entanglement reduces novelty.
uncertainties: The candidate is a compound of several distinct accomplishments (ion gates versus lattice simulators) whose parts may need different recognition.
Choosing which three of four credited names is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The theory of flat bands at the magic angle and the discovery of correlated insulating and superconducting states in twisted bilayer graphene created a very active field of moire quantum matter and a new tuneable platform for strongly correlated physics.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald predicted flat bands; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive first experiments, together with Cao and others not on the list, so the allocation is somewhat constrained by who is credited. A three-person prize looks plausible.
assessment.maturity: Replication across many groups is strong, but the interpretation of the superconductivity and the correlated phases is still developing, so there is a case that recognition is somewhat early.
uncertainties: The mechanism of superconductivity is unsettled.
Credit to early graduate-student and postdoc contributors (e.g. Cao) and other theorists is not resolved here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantized conductance in ballistic point contacts in 1988 was a simple and beautiful demonstration of electron transport through a few quantum channels, foundational for mesoscopic physics and the basis for much of quantum-device physics, including the Landauer picture I know from my own training in mesoscopic transport.
assessment.attribution: Two groups (Delft/Philips and Cambridge) reported the effect simultaneously; the listed names reflect this. Allocation requires including both teams, and the role of theoretical work (Landauer, Buttiker) is not in the list.
assessment.maturity: Very mature and universally confirmed; the risk is that it is old and that the community may regard it as a textbook result rather than one for a late prize.
uncertainties: The long delay since 1988 and the priority between two simultaneous discoveries.
Whether the discovery should be viewed as the main discovery or as a part of the mesoscopic transport family.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Photonic band-gap structures, proposed independently by Yablonovitch and John in 1987, introduced control of spontaneous emission and light propagation through structure and led to photonic crystals and fibers.
assessment.attribution: Yablonovitch and John are the originators; Russell and Noda are major contributors for photonic crystal fibers and nanocavities, so there is a plausible four-person field but I would limit the prize to the two originators.
assessment.maturity: Mature, strongly confirmed and widely used, with an important technological impact; whether the original goal of a complete 3D band gap's applications was fulfilled is partially unresolved.
uncertainties: Competing claims between originators and applied developers (Russell, Noda).
Whether the physics or the technology is the discovery.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube's detection of a diffuse flux of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos in 2013 and of the associated blazar TXS 0506+056 opened neutrino astronomy at PeV energies. This is a new observational window and a major instrument achievement.
assessment.attribution: The decisive work is collective; Halzen led the concept and the collaboration, with Karle and Spiering as other key figures, but the supplied list omits some leaders and the role of AMANDA and the large collaboration complicates a three-person prize. I defer to colleagues in astroparticle physics.
assessment.maturity: Strongly confirmed for the diffuse flux; source identification is still limited to a few objects, so the interpretation is still developing.
uncertainties: Source identification remains incomplete and some associations are only at modest significance.
Attribution is difficult in a large collaboration and I lack expertise in this field.
